chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who buys the foodstuff of a specific town: and if he does not specify for him the foodstuff of that specific town, he may give it from wherever he wishes.

key_terms.بِعَيْنِهَا: In particular / specifically (referring to a specific town or batch)
key_terms.طَعَامَ قَرْيَةٍ: Foodstuff of a town (bulk goods sourced from a specific location)

ai.seo_question: What is the seller's obligation if the buyer does not specify the exact source of the foodstuff purchased?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the principle of *ikhtiyar* (discretion) for the seller in bulk commodity sales when the specific origin or batch is not explicitly defined by the buyer. It reflects the practical commercial norms of early Shia jurisprudence, ensuring flexibility in trade while preventing disputes over unspecified goods. The ruling underscores the importance of clear specification (*tabyin*) in contracts to avoid ambiguity (*gharar*).

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, from Khalid Bin Al Hajjaj,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who buys the foodstuff of a town in particular: ‘And if the foodstuff of a particular town is not mentioned (to the buyers), he can give it from wherever he so desires to’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following:

“About the case of a man who buys foodstuff of a certain town, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If the foodstuff of a certain town exactly is not mentioned he can give it from anywhere he likes . 555
